facility_roles.note: Start: deployment (December 2010). End: first year after the last source reporting operation (December 2016); no shutdown date is published.
facility_roles.quote: It was codeployed with IceCube 2457 m deep in the South Pole glacial ice in December 2010 and is the first such detector operating in the Southern Hemisphere.

intervals.label: deployment with IceCube and commissioning
intervals.note: Deployment in the 2010-11 IceCube construction season; the physics run began on 16 June 2011 (next interval). The month of deployment is December 2010 in every source read.
intervals.quote: DM-Ice17, the first stage of the DM-Ice experimental program, was deployed at the geographic South Pole in December 2010 [36].

intervals.label: primary physics run
intervals.quote: The analysis presented here covers the 3.6 year primary physics run of DM-Ice17 from June 16, 2011 to January 28, 2015.

intervals.label: continued stable operation after the physics run
intervals.note: The December 2016 proceedings say the detectors continued stable operation after the primary run (June 2011 - January 2015) and call DM-Ice17 'operating successfully'; it is the last source read that reports the detectors operating. No end of operation is published.
intervals.quote: The detectors have continued stable operations since.

intervals.label: completed (no end date published)
intervals.note: No source read gives a shutdown date; the programme moved into the joint COSINE-100 run (arXiv:1612.07426) and the 2026 NaI review (arXiv:2607.24448) describes DM-Ice17 in the past tense. The year 2017 is the first year after the last source reporting operation, not a published end date.
intervals.quote: DM-Ice17, the first step in the DM-Ice experimental program, consists of 17 kg of NaI(Tl) located at the South Pole under 2200 m.w.e. overburden of Antarctic glacial ice.

name: DM-Ice17
notes: external.inspire_experiment is null: INSPIRE was not consulted (its rate budget belongs to the supervised importer).

Placement: two crystals, one at the bottom of an IceCube string near the array centre and one about 500 m away towards the edge (arXiv:2607.24448); both are recorded on the single IceCube site record, whose point is the geographic South Pole (precision 2 km, an Atlas convention for the array).
No website: the collaboration's page (dm-ice.physics.wisc.edu) could only be read as a redirect notice.

DM-Ice37, the R&D test-bed of two NaI(Tl) crystals (37 kg) at Boulby, has no physics result of its own and is not recorded as an experiment; DM-Ice250 (the planned 250 kg array) names no host site in the sources read. See the log.
The DM-Ice programme joined KIMS-NaI to form COSINE-100: 'DM-Ice and KIMS-NaI have formed a new collaboration, COSINE-100' (arXiv:1612.07426); the predecessor row is on experiment:cosine-100.

physics_goals.quote: DM-Ice is a phased experimental program using low-background NaI(Tl) crystals with the aim to unambiguously test the claim of dark matter detection by the DAMA experiments.
physics_goals.value: Test, with the same NaI(Tl) target and from the Southern Hemisphere, the annual modulation signal claimed by DAMA/LIBRA

summary.plain: DM-Ice17 was 17 kg of sodium iodide crystals frozen into the Antarctic ice at the South Pole next to the IceCube neutrino detector, a first test in the Southern Hemisphere of the yearly signal DAMA reported. Too small to settle that question, it showed that the ice is a quiet place for such detectors.
summary.technical: Two modules, each an 8.5 kg NaI(Tl) crystal with two photomultipliers in a stainless-steel pressure vessel, co-deployed with IceCube at 2457 m depth (about 2200 m.w.e.). Physics run 16 June 2011 - 28 January 2015, exposure 60.8 kg yr; background 7.9 +- 0.4 counts/day/keV/kg at 6.5-8.0 keVee; no annual modulation in 4-20 keV. The crystals were previously used by NAIAD at Boulby.
